description:
Read the active typed subscription rows on one side of this workspace's own company. Use side=sold for subscriptions the workspace sells to clients, or side=buy for subscriptions it buys from suppliers. This read applies the server's exact monthly amount rule, keeps currencies separate, and does not convert them. Rows with an exclusion_reason stay out of clients, suppliers and totals; excluded counts rows by reason, and each row carries needs_review when it has an exclusion_reason. A read is capped at 500 subscriptions, and rows_truncated says when more exist. On a sold read, `clients[].monthly_total` is each client's live monthly figure, the per-client value. Pass billed_year to add a server-computed billed total per client and currency for that calendar year; `billed_totals[]` pairs with it by `company_id` and currency. The current UTC year ends today; a past year covers the full calendar year. billed_period names the dates and the scope: the total sums only the billed invoices linked to the client's active subscriptions, so an invoice of an ended or replaced subscription, or one with no subscription link, stays out, and the answer must say so. billed_totals_status says whether the result is complete; may_double_count means the period holds a corrected or consolidated invoice (replacing_invoice_count per client), which the total may count next to the invoice it replaces. This total counts issued revenue documents, nets credit notes, keeps currencies separate, and uses each invoice's grand_total. It never changes or replaces the monthly run-rate. Do not calculate a billed total from the newest invoice samples. Sold rows also include up to 12 newest live linked invoices per subscription, each invoice's effective lifecycle status_code, payment_status, paid_amount, balance_due, last_payment_allocation_date and whether a confirmed bank allocation exists, their total count, the workspace's unresolved-customer count and missing-own-company park count (capped at 10,001, which means 10,001 or more), up to five distinct sorted Pennylane customer labels with a count of additional labels, a review_summary that keeps excluded typed rows, unresolved source subscriptions and parked own-company subscriptions separate and names the recorded billing-subscriptions scope refusal when the Pennylane token lacks that scope, and Pennylane's last successful sync and latest completed sync status. Labels are trimmed and omit provider rows with no readable name.

**Every workspace of the person.** With `workspaces: "all_my_workspaces"` — on every call on WhatsApp, and elsewhere when the person asks across all their workspaces — the read also reads each other real workspace the person may read, at most 10 of them, found from the person and never named in the call. `other_workspaces` then holds each one's own subscriptions, clients (for side=sold), suppliers, totals, excluded counts, review_summary, and Pennylane's last successful sync and latest completed sync status for that workspace, and `other_workspaces_skipped` counts the ones past that limit, so every combined figure covers the workspaces read only. `all_workspaces_totals` gives, per currency, the combined monthly total across every workspace read, this one included; `all_workspaces_suppliers` ranks the bought rows across them, each line named by its `workspace_id`; `workspace_order.workspace_ids` lists the workspace blocks largest first. When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

billed_year.description: For a sold-side billed-total read, pass "current" for the current UTC year or a calendar year. The current year runs through today; a past year covers the full year.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

workspaces.description: Which workspaces the read reads. Omit it, or pass "this_workspace", for this workspace alone. Pass "all_my_workspaces" on every call on WhatsApp, and elsewhere when the person asks across all their workspaces: `other_workspaces` then holds each other workspace's own rows, and the all-workspaces fields total and rank across every workspace read.

name: well_list_subscription_rows

monthly_total.description: This client's live monthly total before VAT (HT), in its currency: the per-client monthly figure. `billed_totals[]` pairs with it by company_id and currency.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

monthly_total.description: This client's live monthly total before VAT (HT), in its currency: the per-client monthly figure. `billed_totals[]` pairs with it by company_id and currency.

billing_subscriptions_scope_refusal.description: The diagnostic recorded for the billing-subscriptions scope: "auth_scope_insufficient" means the Pennylane token lacks it and no read of the target has succeeded since; null otherwise.

parked_own_company_subscription_count.description: Pennylane subscriptions parked because the workspace has no own company; 10,001 means 10,001 or more.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

billing_subscriptions_scope_refusal.description: The diagnostic recorded for the billing-subscriptions scope: "auth_scope_insufficient" means the Pennylane token lacks it and no read of the target has succeeded since; null otherwise.

parked_own_company_subscription_count.description: Pennylane subscriptions parked because the workspace has no own company; 10,001 means 10,001 or more.
